extracted.intended_audience: new Scribophile users / writers looking to post and critique work on Scribophile
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for new Scribophile members on how to earn and spend karma, post works for critique, write effective critiques, and participate in the community. Covers posting limits, spotlight mechanics, critique quality expectations, and profile/community features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work definition and length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: A “work” is a single unit of writing, like a single poem, short story, or novel chapter. Each work should be no longer than about 4,000 words; longer work can be posted in parts and linked together during the posting process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect the ~4,000-word limit for individual posts; if your piece is longer, post it in parts and link them together during posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Karma points — how you earn them
rubrics_metrics.description: You earn karma points by writing critiques for the writing of others, and by having other members react positively to your critiques by marking them as constructive, thorough, and so on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You earn more karma points for critiquing work in one of the spotlights versus critiquing work that’s not in one of the spotlights. The longer the critique, the more points you’ll earn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Karma points — how you spend them
rubrics_metrics.description: You spend karma points on posting your writing for critique, giving virtual gifts to other members, and for a few other things around the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It costs 5 karma points to post a new work for critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main Spotlight and other spotlights (point incentives and indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Main Spotlight is a list of work that is currently up for critique. The yellow circle means the work is in a spotlight, and that you’ll earn the most karma points for critiques of this work. After you’ve critiqued a work, you’ll see a green check and the Main Spotlight entry will appear dimmer. There are other spotlights that may award points based on certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Main Spotlight is the easiest way to find works that award the most karma points for critiques; use spotlights to maximize points.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to start a critique (process guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: After you open a work, you can start a critique by clicking the 'Write a critique' button near the top. You can also read the critiques a work has received by scrolling to the bottom of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading other peoples’ critiques can be great insight into how to write effective critiques. If you need more guidance, check the Academy article 'How to Write Great Critiques.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality expectations for critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Critiques should be constructive and provide actionable ways for the author to improve; critiques that consist of bulk without actionable feedback or that break rules are considered poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let the critiquer know what you thought of the critique by clicking reaction buttons (e.g., 'Thorough', 'Encouraging') so they earn more karma. Alert site moderators to poor critiques using the 'Bad critique' button; such alerts are anonymously reviewed and help maintain quality standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaction buttons and rewarding critics
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers can rate critiques using reaction buttons like 'Thorough' or 'Encouraging'; these reactions cause critiquers to earn more karma points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click reaction buttons to reward useful critiques; receiving positive reactions on your critiques also helps you earn more karma points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting process and post management
rubrics_metrics.description: You can post a new work using the 'Post a new work' button; manage your posted writing (post new writing, edit, delete, lock, or unlock your writing) from the posted writing page in the navigation sidebar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The posting process is fairly straightforward, but make sure to respect the 4,000 word limit for individual posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile setup and visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up your personal profile so your readers know a little about you; after you’ve written a little about yourself, you can view your profile and see your followers, who you’re following, groups, scratchpad, gifts, works, critiques, and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A completed profile helps readers learn about you and can help build followers and community connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community participation features and norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in writer’s groups, the Forums, private messages, and leave notes on members’ scratchpads to thank or connect with other writers. See members’ Latest Activity lists and adjust privacy settings as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joining groups and engaging in forums, messages, and scratchpad notes are recommended ways to network, find beta readers, and become part of the community.
